claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,q), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard P-256 generator P, recover x, the parallel Pollard rho algorithm in proof.md (P=262144 walks sharing one r=64 transition table with full-size uniform multipliers and starts and wrapping residues, Montgomery-domain batched P-256 additions with analytically bounded field arithmetic including six modular subtractions per addition, shared distinguished-point table) succeeds with probability at least 0.3995 using at most 2^129.02 total computation, with all P-256 arithmetic charged as justified instructions divided by the borrowed C=1000 normalization (H=0), including preprocessing and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^105.59 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^24 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, quantum steps, or random-oracle premises. Success relies on the supported shared-function random-mapping (standard Teske regime, covering table occupancy; no hash heuristic), the only heuristic, disclosed and supported in proof.md. This is an analytic best-known-attack cost analysis, not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Run the identical multi-walk attack path on the fixed prime-order toy curve (n=9883) and measure success rate against the birthday prediction. This does not establish production curve behavior or cost bounds.

title: p256-ecdlp: parallel batched rho, r=64, standard-regime wrapping walk, at 39%+ success
